acts.name: COLD_OPEN
acts.hook_objective: Drop viewer into September 2019: a $47 billion company that can't pay its rent in 30 days.

retention_beats.event: Display $47,000,000,000 valuation alongside internal bank statement showing company running out of cash by November.
WeWork was losing $219,000 every single hour, 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.

acts.name: THE_PROMISE
acts.hook_objective: Frame the central mystery: why did the smartest money in finance believe an office sublease landlord was Google?

retention_beats.event: How did a barefoot entrepreneur selling partitioned drywall convince Wall Street he had discovered a new state of human consciousness?
Paper tear transition from glossy tech keynote to dusty landlord rent ledger.

acts.name: THE_DREAM
acts.hook_objective: Establish Adam Neumann's hypnotic charisma, post-2008 freelance boom, and the founding of WeWork.

retention_beats.event: Adam Neumann puppet in SoHo: from baby knee pads (Krawlers) to GreenDesk.
Free beer on tap, neon quotes ('Hustle Harder'), fruit water, and communal desks.
Pitching real estate as a 'physical social network' to capture tech valuation multiples (20x revenue instead of 1x EBITDA).
The arrival of Benchmark Capital and early venture capital validations.

acts.name: THE_MACHINE
acts.hook_objective: Explain the mechanics: The 12-minute meeting with Masayoshi Son, SoftBank's billions, and the asset-liability death trap.

retention_beats.event: Masa Son's 12-minute tour: 'Who wins, the smart guy or the crazy guy? You are not crazy enough.'
The $4.4B SoftBank firehose: WeWork opening a new floor every single day worldwide.
Visual analogy: Asset-Liability Mismatch. Signing 15-year fixed leases while renting out month-to-month hot desks.
The invention of 'Community Adjusted EBITDA'—stripping out the rent from a business that only pays rent.

acts.name: THE_CRACK
acts.hook_objective: August 14, 2019: The Form S-1 is filed. The curtain falls. The absurd self-dealing receipts.

retention_beats.event: The S-1 dedication page: 'To the energy of we'. Analysts open the document and burst out laughing.
The $5.9 million 'We' trademark payment: Adam sells a two-letter word to his own company.
Landlord kickbacks: Adam personally buys buildings and leases them back to WeWork.
The $60M Gulfstream G650 jet, wave pool investments (Wavegarden), and Rebekah's succession veto.

acts.name: THE_COLLISION
acts.hook_objective: The 33-day death spiral: Valuation plummets from $47B to $10B, debt vanishes, board mutiny.

retention_beats.event: Scott Galloway's 'WeWTF' analysis goes viral. Wall Street institutional buyers flee the roadshow.
The $6 billion JPMorgan trap: If the IPO fails to raise $3B, the credit line evaporates to $0.
September 17: IPO postponed. Cash calculation shows bankruptcy in 30 days.
September 24: Board votes Adam out. Masa Son pulls the plug.

acts.name: THE_AFTERMATH
acts.hook_objective: The rescue, the litigation, the pandemic, and the final Chapter 11 bankruptcy.

retention_beats.event: SoftBank bails out WeWork at an $8B valuation, and Neumann walks away with hundreds of millions.
Delaware Chancery Court battle: Neumann walks with $480M cash out in 2021 settlement.
November 2023: Chapter 11 filing in New Jersey. Original shareholders completely wiped out.

acts.name: THE_PAYOFF
acts.hook_objective: Deliver the definitive, unforgettable insight on venture capital madness and bridge to the next episode.

retention_beats.event: A desk is not a software algorithm. You cannot scale a concrete building at zero marginal cost.
WeWork wasn't alone in turning physical commodities into tech mirages. Next: The electric truck powered by gravity.
